history.period: Centuries old; no reliable founding date
history.summary: Hilltop shrine complex in central Dewas housing the Devi Chamunda Mata Temple and the Devi Tulja Bhavani Temple (locally called Badi Maa and Choti Maa), plus shrines to Kalika Mata, Hanuman, Bhairav Baba and Annapurna. Legend calls it a Rakt Peeth, where blood from Mata Sati fell, and tradition holds the idols are self-manifested. 'Shankh Duvar' (conch gate) refers to the entrance area of the Tekri; the site is reached by stairs, a sliding path or ropeway, and draws large crowds during Navaratri. Note: no reliable source gives a founding date, so the summary here is approximate.

name: Mata Tekri Shankh Duvar
town_description: Dewas is a city in western Madhya Pradesh, about 35 km northeast of Indore on the Indore-Bhopal highway (NH-47). It is an industrial and commercial centre with roots as a former princely state capital, and the Tekri hill in the middle of the city is its best-known landmark. Dewas sits between Indore, Ujjain and Omkareshwar, making it a convenient pilgrimage stop in the Malwa region.
